entries.name: Janet McCloud

expected.charges: Illegal fishing in violation of Washington state regulations — 1965 Nisqually fish-in
expected.sentence: 6 days county jail (1965 conviction); hunger strike

updates.charges: Obstructing a public officer during the October 13, 1965 Nisqually fish-in
updates.convicted: No — acquitted by jury in January 1969
updates.sentence: Arrested October 13, 1965; acquitted by a jury in January 1969. Laura McCloud recalled that the defendants posted bail within hours of arrest, while the 2003 Seattle Post-Intelligencer obituary reports six days in jail and a hunger strike. These conflicting custody accounts remain unresolved; no exact release day or verified six-day total is assigned. October 1965 release is retained at month precision. Janet McCloud also described a separate 1966 arrest and hunger strike with Edith McCloud and Dick Gregory; that episode must not be conflated with this prosecution.

entries.rationale: Correct false conviction and illegal-fishing charge using contemporaneous docket and firsthand trial account. January1969 acquittal independently corroborated by HankAdams archive description republished by WAagency. Preserve release month shared by both conflicting accounts; remove disputed six-day exact override without inventing replacement.
